## Incahuasi Island in the Uyuni Salt Flat: cacti and a white horizon

[Incahuasi](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/) is a rocky island rising above the almost level surface of Bolivia's [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). Tall cacti grow on its slopes, and the upper trail opens up views of the white salt plain stretching to the horizon.

For travelers, it is one of Uyuni's most recognizable stops. After driving across flat salt for a long distance, a rocky outcrop with living vegetation comes into view. Here you can examine cacti, the shape of the ancient island formation, and the unusual contrast between rock and salt.

## Why is Incahuasi called an island?

Incahuasi stands above an enormous salt flat formed on the site of ancient lakes of the high-altitude Altiplano. When water covered the surrounding lowlands, elevated areas like this were islands. As the lakes changed and salt deposits accumulated, the rocky hills remained protruding above the white plain.

Today, Incahuasi looks like a stone island surrounded by salt. It is not an ordinary island enclosed by seawater or a settlement on an ocean shore.

The contrast is particularly striking from the salt flat's surface: an almost level, pale plain stretches around you, while the island itself has dark rocks, an uneven trail, and plants.

## Why giant cacti grow on the island

Tall cacti grow in the island's rocky substrate, creating a distinctive silhouette against the salt flat. They are adapted to dryness, strong sunshine, and temperature changes. Some specimens grow several meters tall.

They grow slowly, so damaging a stem, trampling young plants, or cutting pieces from a cactus can harm the site for years. Use the existing path to explore and avoid entering the vegetation.

Large cacti make striking photographs with the distant horizon behind them. When photographing from elevated ground, maintain stable footing on rocks and avoid fragile edges.

## What can you see from the Incahuasi trail?

The main reward for climbing is the panoramic view of the salt flat. The pale surface often displays polygonal salt patterns. In the dry season, their geometric outlines are clearly visible; in the rainy season, some areas may be covered by water, reflecting the clouds.

Changing surface conditions also affect **whether vehicles can reach the island**. When water is high, parts of the route become impassable, so the visit may be replaced by another stop in Uyuni. The island's inclusion in a promotional itinerary should not be taken as a guarantee of access in any weather.

## How the island features in jeep tours

On the [three-day Ada Tours Uyuni Salt Flat tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/), Incahuasi is scheduled for the third day. After sunrise on the salt flat, visits to [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/) and the natural [Ojos del Salar](/bolivia/place/ojos-del-salar/) water holes, the route continues to the island. Entry to Incahuasi is charged separately at **30 bolivianos**.

On the [12-day Peru and Bolivia with Uyuni itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/), the island is associated with the excursion day on the salt flat, which also includes a look at the local salt industry and scenic stops.

The same place appearing on different itineraries does not mean the same services: meals, entry tickets, and the order of stops are determined by each particular tour.

## Incahuasi and other Uyuni sights

The journey is often combined with [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/), where salt extraction and processing are demonstrated, and the [Ojos del Salar](/bolivia/place/ojos-del-salar/), small water openings in the salt crust.

Other routes may visit [Tahua](/bolivia/place/tahua/) and the [Tunupa Volcano](/bolivia/place/tunupa-volcano/) area. All these places belong to the wider geography of Uyuni, but require different travel times.

## What to consider before visiting

The salt flat lies at approximately 3,650 m above sea level. Sunshine reflects brightly from the salt, so UV-protective dark glasses, a hat, and sunscreen are useful. Wear closed-toe shoes for the rocky path.

The ascent may be short, but altitude can make it noticeably harder than a walk at sea level. Follow the designated trail and rules protecting the vegetation.

## Frequently asked questions about Incahuasi

### Is the island really in the middle of salt?

Yes. It is a rocky elevation rising above the Uyuni Salt Flat.

### Can I visit Incahuasi during the rainy season?

Access is sometimes possible, but when the salt surface is flooded, vehicles may be restricted or prevented from traveling there. It depends on actual conditions.

### Are there really large cacti on the island?

Yes. Tall cacti are one of Incahuasi's main natural features.

### Is the island ticket included in the three-day jeep tour?

On the [three-day Ada Tours itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-uyuni-salt-flats-jeep-tour-3-days/), the 30-boliviano entry fee is listed as a separate expense.

## Tours visiting Incahuasi Island: what is actually included?

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. [Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/), also known as Incawasi, forms part of the main itinerary of the [11-day Bolivia tour with Titicaca, La Paz, Uyuni, and Torotoro](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/). It is not merely listed as an optional activity: a specific stop appears in the program on **day 6**.

The island stands in the [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) salt plain. In dry weather, the salt flat looks like an endless white surface, with the rocky, cactus-covered hill standing out dramatically. The main reason to stop is to walk up the slope and view the salt plain from above. This panorama offers a completely different perspective from photographs taken at salt level.

## Day 6: from Colchani to Incahuasi

On this day, travelers fly to Uyuni and begin a vehicle route through the salt flat. Among the first stops are the [Train Cemetery](/bolivia/place/uyuni-train-cemetery/) and [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/), where they learn about salt processing. They then drive through [Ojos del Salar](/bolivia/place/ojos-del-salar/) and the Playa Blanca area.

At **Incahuasi**, the itinerary includes observing rocky sections, large cacti, and natural cavities. From the elevated viewpoint there is an expansive view of the salt plain. This stop is especially interesting because it shows that Uyuni is more than a flat white expanse: a rocky island with its own ecosystem and vegetation has survived in the middle of the salt.

After the island, the route travels south across the salt flat toward Lípez. The [Ollagüe Volcano](/bolivia/place/ollague-volcano/) is visible in the distance, and the journey continues into the [Eduardo Avaroa National Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). The day ends at [Laguna Cañapa](/bolivia/place/laguna-canapa/), [Laguna Hedionda](/bolivia/place/laguna-hedionda/), and [Laguna Honda](/bolivia/place/laguna-honda/), where flamingos can be seen. The overnight stay is in an expedition-style lodge.

Thus, the Incahuasi visit is part of **a full journey across the salt flat and onward into Lípez**, not a short trip from town returning immediately after taking photographs.

## What makes Incahuasi interesting?

The island differs from the surrounding plain in several immediately visible ways. Instead of level salt, the ground is rocky. Column-shaped cacti rise above visitors. From the viewpoint, there is an immense white horizon with distant mountains. These features explain why Incahuasi is often a destination in its own right on a Uyuni route.

The word "island" relates to the region's history and its appearance as a rise within a former lake. **In the dry season, the island is surrounded by salt, not open water.** During the rains, some of the salt flat becomes covered in water, creating Uyuni's famous mirror effect. Although beautiful, excessive water can make the island inaccessible by vehicle.

Read more about the place on the [Incahuasi Island page](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/). When choosing a tour, the practical question is whether you can visit the island and continue toward the lagoons given the season, driving conditions, and total trip duration.

## When to choose an itinerary visiting the island

Uyuni changes appearance with the seasons. During dry months, the solid salt surface usually permits routes to remote places, including Incahuasi. During the rains, water reflects clouds, but **access to the island is sometimes restricted**. Specialist guides to the salt flat confirm this. A full mirror effect and road access to every island cannot both be guaranteed.

Distinguish between two aims when choosing dates:

- **An Incahuasi panorama and a walk among cacti.** This depends on vehicle access and an open walking path.
- **Uyuni's reflective salt surface.** This requires a shallow layer of water and suitable weather, which may lead to changes in the route.

The specific Ada Tours itinerary provides for a stop on the island. However, natural conditions and driving safety depend on the situation at the time. The general tour terms allow the sequence of excursions to change while preserving the program. If Incahuasi is your essential priority, discuss it when selecting dates and an itinerary rather than turning a weather-dependent possibility into a promise.

## How to choose a journey featuring Incahuasi

The [11-day itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) combines several parts of Bolivia. Before Uyuni, it visits [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), [Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/), and [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). After the salt flat, the route continues to high-altitude lagoons, desert scenery, and Torotoro National Park. Incahuasi is one natural stop in a larger trip.

If your main goal is the salt flat and Incahuasi's cacti, compare itineraries by the actual time spent in Uyuni, stopping points, and transfers. The word "Uyuni" in a tour title **does not prove the island is included**. Search the [Bolivia tours catalog](/bolivia/tour/) and [Bolivia adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/bolivia/) for suitable formats, checking the actual main route.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_priklyucheniya_v_bolivii}}

## Practical tips for visiting the island

Walking up the rocky slope is different from traveling across level salt. Wear closed-toe shoes with stable soles, sunglasses, a hat, and bring water and an extra layer for wind. Strong sunlight at altitude and over the exposed salt surface is particularly noticeable. Walk the rocky trail at a relaxed pace and follow vegetation conservation rules.

The [11-day tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/) includes land transport, admission tickets, excursions with a Russian-speaking guide, and meals during the Uyuni stage. Airport taxes, tips, and additional lunches and dinners outside the included package are listed among excluded expenses.

## Frequently asked questions about tours to Incahuasi

### On which day is the island visited?

**Day 6** of the [11-day journey through Bolivia](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/). The group first arrives in the Uyuni area, visits [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/) and the salt flat, then stops on Incahuasi.

### Is it an included or optional stop?

Incahuasi appears among the **main itinerary destinations**. It is not listed only as an optional activity. Actual access, however, depends on conditions on the salt flat.

### Is Incahuasi an island in a lake?

In the dry season, it is a rocky rise amid salt. During rains, water may surround it and create mirror reflections. The word "island" does not imply a permanent boat crossing.

### What is the difference between Uyuni and Incahuasi?

[Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) is an enormous salt plain, while [Incahuasi](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/) is a particular rocky outcrop within it, known for cacti and a viewpoint. A salt flat itinerary can also exist without a stop on the island.

### Where does the tour go after the island?

On the confirmed itinerary, the journey continues into the [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/) and to high-altitude lagoons, with an overnight stay at an expedition lodge. This forms part of a multi-day journey, so the day's stop should be considered within the entire transport schedule.

## Places to visit in Bolivia: choosing destinations and planning a route

Bolivia offers several very different geographical regions. The Uyuni Salt Flat and colorful lagoons are trips through the southern Altiplano; Lake Titicaca and La Paz offer high-altitude cultural routes; Sucre and Potosí are connected with colonial history, while the forests in the north and east require different transport and a different pace. The main mistake when choosing attractions is assuming they are neighboring stops simply because they lie in one country.

Here you can explore {{catalog.placesCountPhrase}} in Bolivia individually. The [Bolivia tours catalog](/bolivia/tour/) shows which places actually feature in existing itineraries.

## La Paz and Titicaca: city, archaeology, and lake

[La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/) is a convenient starting point for several Altiplano destinations. Changes in elevation are noticeable within the city and surrounding area, so a busy excursion day immediately after arrival is not suitable for everyone. Leave time to adapt and choose moderate physical activity.

For ancient architecture, visit [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), an archaeological UNESCO World Heritage Site. Stone structures survive around the ceremonial center; the [Gate of the Sun](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku-gate-of-the-sun/) and [Kalasasaya Temple](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku-kalasasaya/) allow you to examine individual monuments. A meaningful guided excursion is more useful than briefly stopping at a few famous photo spots.

On the shore of [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/) is [Copacabana](/bolivia/place/copacabana/), associated with boat journeys to the [Island of the Sun](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/) and [Island of the Moon](/bolivia/place/isla-de-la-luna/). Account for boat transfers, local schedules, and altitude. Choose walks on the islands that suit your abilities: even a moderate climb feels different at this elevation than at sea level.

[Moon Valley](/bolivia/place/moon-valley-la-paz/) is a short nature excursion near the city route, ideal for seeing erosion landforms without traveling far. It does not replace the dramatic, multi-day landscapes of southwestern Bolivia.

## Uyuni: the salt flat and its surroundings

[Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) is the starting point for exploring the salt flat. During the dry season, a white salt plain with geometric patterns dominates the landscape. When water remains on certain sections, reflections of the sky become possible, but conditions depend on rainfall and route accessibility. No particular effect can be guaranteed for a travel date.

[Incahuasi Island](/bolivia/place/incahuasi-island/) is a rocky rise with cacti amid the salt landscape. Whether it can be visited depends on driving conditions. Other routes may include [Colchani](/bolivia/place/colchani/), the [Train Cemetery](/bolivia/place/uyuni-train-cemetery/), and small local settlements. These are different stops, and their inclusion should be checked against each specific tour.

A short itinerary may be enough for photographing and seeing the salt flat, but traveling to the southern lagoons and volcanic landscapes requires considerably more time. Differences in accommodation and hours spent in vehicles are particularly significant.

## The colorful lagoons of the southern Altiplano: an expedition route

[Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/), [Laguna Verde](/bolivia/place/laguna-verde/), [Laguna Blanca](/bolivia/place/laguna-blanca/), and other high-altitude lakes lie in demanding natural conditions. Their colors and appearance differ, while water levels, wind, and light change what you see at each location.

Many itineraries pass through the [Eduardo Avaroa Reserve](/bolivia/place/eduardo-avaroa-national-reserve/). You can find the [Sol de Mañana geysers](/bolivia/place/sol-de-manana-geysers/), [Polques Hot Springs](/bolivia/place/polques-hot-springs/), desert landscapes, and volcanoes here. Do not choose solely from photographs: understand how many hours the road takes, where you will sleep, and which altitudes you will experience.

The [Siloli Desert](/bolivia/place/siloli-desert/) and [Árbol de Piedra](/bolivia/place/arbol-de-piedra/) are nature stops in the same region. They should not be considered separate excursions available on any day from La Paz. They are part of a substantial transport route across the southwest.

## Sucre and Potosí: cities with different histories

[Sucre](/bolivia/place/sucre/) appeals for its white façades, historic cityscape, and museums. Its colonial center is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Plan time to walk through the neighborhoods instead of restricting the visit to a transit lunch.

[Potosí](/bolivia/place/potosi/) is associated with silver mining and South America's colonial economy. It sits high above sea level, and exertion should be considered separately. Visiting mining sites requires particular attention to safety and the specific terms of an excursion.

These two cities can be combined in a historical itinerary, but should not automatically be added to a Uyuni trip without calculating travel time.

## Eastern and northern Bolivia: different natural conditions

[Santa Cruz](/bolivia/place/santa-cruz/) and [Samaipata](/bolivia/place/samaipata/) introduce a side of Bolivia that differs from the Altiplano. The El Fuerte de Samaipata archaeological complex is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, while [Amboró National Park](/bolivia/place/amboro-national-park/) attracts visitors interested in forests, birds, and nature walks.

A completely different destination is [Rurrenabaque](/bolivia/place/rurrenabaque/) and [Madidi National Park](/bolivia/place/madidi-national-park/) in the north. These areas are chosen for forest ecosystems and wildlife observation. Check the rainy season, road and river logistics, and regulations for visiting protected areas.

[Torotoro](/bolivia/place/torotoro/), with its canyons and caves, is best treated as a separate nature stage. In particular, [Umajalanta Cave](/bolivia/place/umajalanta-cave/) and [El Vergel Canyon](/bolivia/place/el-vergel-canyon/) require sufficient driving time and suitable walking conditions.

## Combining places without an overloaded schedule

For a short holiday, choose one main geographical region, such as La Paz and Titicaca or Uyuni. On a longer journey, high-altitude cities can be combined with the salt flat, but the pace should allow for acclimatization.

If you want a nature itinerary without remaining at extreme altitude throughout, consider [Samaipata](/bolivia/place/samaipata/), [Amboró](/bolivia/place/amboro-national-park/), and northern forests rather than adding them to every overview of the highlands.

Compare not only attraction names but also how to travel between them. Ada Tours helps arrange the order of visits, accommodation, and spare travel time based on the selected itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about Bolivia's attractions

### Which places should I choose for a first visit to Bolivia?

Visitors often begin with [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), [Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/), and [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). For a shorter journey, however, it is better to choose one or two neighboring areas and allow time for transfers and adjusting to altitude.

### When can you see the sky reflected on the Uyuni Salt Flat?

The mirror effect depends on water remaining on the surface during the rainy season. It depends on actual rainfall, access to the relevant sections, and weather on the day of the excursion.

### How is a visit to Uyuni different from a tour of the colored lagoons?

The salt flat can be visited on a shorter itinerary. The colorful lagoons and volcanic regions of the southern Altiplano usually involve a separate off-road stage, remote overnight stays, and greater physical demands.

### Can I travel in Bolivia without high-altitude excursions?

Yes. For lower, more humid natural areas, consider [Santa Cruz](/bolivia/place/santa-cruz/), [Amboró](/bolivia/place/amboro-national-park/), or [Madidi](/bolivia/place/madidi-national-park/). You should still check the actual elevation and travel arrangements for each place.

## The Island of the Moon on Titicaca: Iñak Uyu Temple and Inca heritage

The [Island of the Moon](/bolivia/place/isla-de-la-luna/) is on the Bolivian side of [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/), near the larger [Island of the Sun](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/). On its slopes are remains of the Inca architectural complex of Iñak Uyu, associated with religious traditions of the Inca state and the lives of women chosen for service in courts and temples.

The island is also known as **Koati**. It is much quieter than large lakeside towns, and visiting combines a boat journey, archaeology, and an introduction to the local community.

## Where the island is and how to reach it

The Island of the Moon lies east of the Island of the Sun, on Titicaca's Bolivian side. It is generally visited by boat as part of an island excursion departing from [Copacabana](/bolivia/place/copacabana/) or another port on the lake. Boat schedules and the order of stops depend on the selected route.

Lake Titicaca lies approximately 3,812 meters above sea level. Even a simple ascent from the boat landing to the ancient structures may require a slower pace. Avoid planning a packed walking program immediately after arriving rapidly from lower altitude.

## What remains of Iñak Uyu Temple

The island's main historic attraction is **Iñak Uyu (Iñakuyu)**, also known as the Temple of the Moon or "Palace of the Virgins of the Sun." The architectural complex is associated with the *acllawasi* institution, where selected women were trained in various activities and took part in Inca religious life.

You can see walls, interior spaces, stepped features, and trapezoid-shaped niches typical of Inca architecture. The stone buildings stand on a slope above the water, and the surrounding scenery remains an important part of the experience.

Historians have proposed different reconstructions of the purposes of individual rooms and details of ceremonial life. The cultural and religious significance of the complex can be stated confidently, but not every popular legend should be treated as an established archaeological fact.

## Island of the Moon and Island of the Sun: what to compare

The [Island of the Sun](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/) is known for an Inca staircase, a sacred spring, ancient structures, and views across Titicaca. The Island of the Moon is smaller, and Iñak Uyu is its main reason to visit. Together, the two sites illustrate the sacred geography of the Inca era around the lake.

Do not confuse their names: these are separate islands, each with its own landing and monuments. Visiting both requires time for the boat crossing, attention to community regulations, and suitable weather.

## The Island of the Moon on an Ada Tours itinerary

On the [11-day Bolivia itinerary](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/), the Island of the Moon is visited the day after exploring Huatajata and Tiwanaku archaeology. A hydrofoil journey is scheduled from Cocotoni Bay to the Island of the Moon and Iñak Uyu Temple.

The itinerary then continues to the [Island of the Sun](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/), [Copacabana](/bolivia/place/copacabana/), and finally a road transfer to [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/). This is the specific order of visits on the selected tour, not a universal pattern for every trip on Titicaca.

The visit concerns the role of women in Inca culture, weaving traditions, and other activities. The scope of museum or historical interpretation should follow the tour description, without inventing meetings, ceremonies, or services that are not included.

## Practical visiting tips

Comfortable shoes for stone steps, sun protection for the intense high-altitude sunlight, and warm clothing in case of wind are useful. The duration of the walk depends on altitude, the route, and the time available before the next boat crossing.

For a journey through [Bolivia](/bolivia/), the island pairs well with [Huatajata](/bolivia/place/huatajata/), [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/), and other lake destinations. If you also plan to visit the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), allocate your days between the lake and more distant nature regions in advance.

## Frequently asked questions about the Island of the Moon

### Is the Island of the Moon in Bolivia?

Yes, on the Bolivian side of Titicaca, close to the Island of the Sun.

### What is Iñak Uyu?

It is an archaeological complex from the Inca period, associated with religious traditions and the activities of women selected for particular responsibilities.

### Can I visit the Islands of the Sun and Moon on one trip?

Yes. Suitable boat routes combine both islands. Agree on timing and the order of visits beforehand.

### Is the island suitable for a quick walk?

The walk is relatively short, but at high altitude. Allow enough time for the ascent from the shore.

## Which Ada Tours itinerary visits the Island of the Moon?

The [Island of the Moon](/bolivia/place/isla-de-la-luna/) (Isla de la Luna, Koati) lies on the Bolivian side of [Lake Titicaca](/bolivia/place/lake-titicaca-bolivia/). Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with **the island as a main visit**, rather than merely an optional excursion. This distinction matters: neighboring itineraries may visit the Island of the Sun without arranging a landing on the Island of the Moon.

The current route is [Bolivia in 11 Days: Titicaca, La Paz, Uyuni, and Torotoro](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/). Part of **day 4** is devoted to the island. The journey begins in Santa Cruz and continues through [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/) and [Huatajata](/bolivia/place/huatajata/). After Titicaca come [La Paz](/bolivia/place/la-paz/), the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), high-altitude lagoons, and [Torotoro](/bolivia/place/torotoro/).

**If your main goal is Iñak Uyu Temple, choose an itinerary explicitly listing the Island of the Moon.** The phrase "Lake Titicaca tour" alone does not mean both islands are included.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_priklyucheniya_v_bolivii}}

## How the Island of the Moon day works

On the 11-day itinerary, a short transfer to Cocotoni Bay follows breakfast. From here, the group takes a hydrofoil across the lake. The first island stop is **the Island of the Moon and Iñak Uyu Temple of the Virgins of the Sun**. The guide explains women's roles in Inca society, religious rituals, crafts, and food-processing traditions. The temple's architecture includes distinctive stone openings, stepped features, and trapezoid-shaped elements.

The hydrofoil then travels to the [Island of the Sun](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/). There, the Great Inca Stairway and the Sacred Spring, associated with local beliefs, are included. Lunch at Uma Kollu restaurant and a visit to a small craft market are also planned for that day.

After visiting the islands, travelers continue by boat to [Copacabana](/bolivia/place/copacabana/). The day's schedule includes the basilica, the shrine of the Black Virgin, and the market. The group then travels by road to La Paz, crossing the Tiquina Strait.

This is a day combining **two islands, a lakeside town, and an onward transfer**. The time available at each monument is limited by the overall schedule. It suits travelers who want to see several important Titicaca sites within an extensive journey across Bolivia.

## Why visit Iñak Uyu?

Official Bolivian tourism materials identify the Island of the Moon with **Iñak Uyu Temple**, linked to the "Virgins of the Sun" tradition. Its archaeological heritage demonstrates that Inca civilization was not confined to large mountain cities and palaces: sacred buildings also stood on islands in the high-altitude lake.

The island's smaller scale is part of its appeal. There is no bustling city center; the experience is shaped by stone architecture, island slopes, and panoramas of Titicaca. Surrounded by water, it is easier to appreciate why the lake and its sanctuaries acquired such significance in local beliefs.

The purpose of the visit differs markedly from exploring [Tiwanaku](/bolivia/place/tiwanaku/). Tiwanaku belongs to an earlier, distinct Andean civilization, whereas Iñak Uyu is understood through Inca heritage. These stops complement rather than replace one another.

## Island of the Moon or Island of the Sun: which to choose?

| Place | Main focus |
|---|---|
| [Island of the Moon](/bolivia/place/isla-de-la-luna/) | Iñak Uyu and religious traditions |
| [Island of the Sun](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/) | Sacred stairway, spring, and hillside trails |
| [Copacabana](/bolivia/place/copacabana/) | Basilica and lakeside town life |

The Island of the Sun offers more route and stop options. Our other itineraries visit it, including the [12-day Peru and Bolivia journey](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/) and the [15-day route including Altiplano lakes](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/). **Neither of these two itineraries specifies a stop on the Island of the Moon.** They suit a different combination of experiences: Machu Picchu, Bolivian Titicaca, Uyuni, and, on the longer tour, the colorful lagoons.

If you want to see both islands on one trip, choose the specific 11-day itinerary. If a wider combination of Peru and Bolivia is the priority, see the [Bolivia tours catalog](/bolivia/tour/) and compare the actual stops, days, and water transport.

## Preparing for a trip on Titicaca

Titicaca lies approximately **3,812 meters above sea level**. Even relaxed walking feels different here from the coast: strong sunshine combines with cool air, and cold winds are possible on the water. For the island day, bring comfortable closed-toe shoes, extra warm clothing, sun protection, and water.

The day involves several transfers between vehicles and boats and landings at historic sites. It is important to look at **the whole chain of transfers**, not only the duration of the boat journey. Boarding conditions, stop durations, and the vessel's route are determined by the actual itinerary.

For high-altitude travel, discuss your health and any personal limitations with a qualified professional in advance, especially if the journey begins almost immediately after arriving from low altitude. This applies to the entire [Bolivia journey](/bolivia/), not only one island.

## Frequently asked questions about tours visiting the Island of the Moon

### Can I visit the Island of the Moon and Island of the Sun on the same day?

**Yes.** On the [11-day Bolivia tour](/bolivia/tour/bolivia-titicaca-uyuni-la-paz-11-days/), day 4 includes both islands, followed by Copacabana and a transfer to La Paz. This is an excursion day with multiple stops, not a separate free day on the island.

### What is the island's main attraction?

**Iñak Uyu Temple**, associated with Inca religious traditions. Its stone architecture and history make the Island of the Moon chiefly a cultural and historical stop. For comparison, see the [neighboring Island of the Sun](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/).

### Is the Island of the Moon included in every tour visiting Lake Titicaca?

**No.** For example, the [12-day Peru–Bolivia itinerary](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-12-days/) and its [15-day version](/multi-country/tour/peru-bolivia-uyuni-lakes-15-days/) include the Island of the Sun but do not specify landing on the Island of the Moon. Choose by the exact program for the day.

### Do I need a separate transfer to the Island of the Moon?

On the featured 11-day itinerary, **water travel is part of the sequence for day 4**: transfer to Cocotoni Bay, hydrofoil to the islands, then Copacabana and La Paz. The conditions for an independent journey outside this tour are not established by this offer.

### Is this day suitable for a holiday focused only on relaxing by the lake?

The itinerary is quite busy, with island monuments, sightseeing in Copacabana, and travel to La Paz. For a relaxed stay on Titicaca, assess the program and duration of stops separately. The [catalog of tours visiting the Island of the Sun as a main destination](/bolivia/place/isla-del-sol/tour/) includes other ways to combine the lake with a longer Andean journey.
